summary: Google's Python library that uses LLMs to pull structured data from text and links every result to its exact source location.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: LangExtract is a Python library for extracting structured information from unstructured text using LLMs. You describe what to extract and give a few examples; it returns consistent results, each mapped to its exact place in the source text, and can render an interactive HTML view.
sixtySeconds.problem: Asking an LLM to extract data gives inconsistent, hard-to-verify results, especially on long documents. LangExtract enforces a schema from your examples and grounds every extraction in the source.
whoFor: Teams building review tools for extracted facts
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for source grounding, reliable structured output, long-document handling and support for Gemini, OpenAI and local Ollama models.
requirements: An API key for cloud models such as Gemini or OpenAI (not needed for local Ollama models)

overview: Define a prompt and a few-shot example with lx.data.ExampleData and lx.data.Extraction, then call lx.extract with your text and a model_id such as gemini-3.5-flash, the recommended default.
Save results with lx.io.save_annotated_documents and create an interactive HTML review page with lx.visualize. Long documents are chunked and processed in parallel over multiple passes.
Set LANGEXTRACT_API_KEY (environment variable or .env file) for cloud models. A live demo runs on Hugging Face Spaces. The library is Apache 2.0 licensed.
limitations: Inferred information should still be checked

steps.title: Set your API key for cloud models
Build and run
steps.code:
docker build -t langextract .
docker run --rm -e LANGEXTRACT_API_KEY="your-api-key" langextract python your_script.py

environment.name: LANGEXTRACT_API_KEY
environment.description: Needed for cloud models like Gemini or OpenAI.

firstRun.title: Try the live demo
firstRun.body: Run grounded extraction on Romeo and Juliet in your browser via the demo link in the README.

tutorial.title: Extract characters and emotions from text
tutorial.useCase: Run a small grounded extraction with a few-shot example.

steps.title: Define the task and an example
Run the extraction
steps.code:
result = lx.extract(
    text_or_documents="Lady Juliet gazed longingly at the stars, her heart aching for Romeo",
    prompt_description=prompt,
    examples=examples,
    model_id="gemini-3.5-flash",
)

tutorial.expected: Structured extractions with their positions in the text, plus an HTML view.
